description:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

This role is preferred office-based to support in-person mentorship and collaboration across internal and partner teams. We’re also open to Benchling employees who are currently remote.

ROLE OVERVIEW

Benchling is looking for a Partner Enablement Manager to help our implementation partners deliver Benchling in pharmaceutical and life science accounts.

You'll train partners in live and virtual sessions, help run partner certification, and observe and coach partners on real projects. You'll bring what you learn back to the CX Enablement team so we can improve our courses. When it works, partners are ready faster, customers go live with confidence no matter who implements, and fewer partner-caused issues reach Support and Professional Services.

This role is a step into enablement for someone who already has experience with Benchling and enjoys teaching others (for example by walking customers through issues, writing knowledge articles, or onboarding new teammates.) You'll work with CX Enablement, Professional Services, Product, the Partners team, and with partner organizations directly. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports.

 

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Train partners directly through live and virtual sessions, such as onboarding cohorts, workshops, and product deep dives, for both subcontracted and direct partner delivery teams

  • Help administer partner certification, including tracking progress and supporting partners through it

  • Gather feedback from partners on where their teams struggle, and work through it with the rest of the CX Enablement team to decide what to improve or build

  • Build partner-specific coursework where it’s needed, and work with the CX Enablement team to bring it into certification pathways

  • Support Professional Services in running subcontracted and direct partner programs by tracking partner readiness and flagging risks early

  • Observe partners on real work, give feedback, and coach them directly on improvements

  • Help prepare partners for new product releases, working with Product and CX Enablement so partners are ready alongside internal teams

  • Report on defined partner readiness measures, such as time to certification and partner-caused support issues, to the enablement team and Professional Services leadership

 

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • Experience teaching Benchling to others, such as through customer calls, escalations, knowledge articles, or onboarding new teammates

  • Hands-on experience supporting or implementing Benchling, with a deep working knowledge of the platform

  • Comfortable presenting to technical and scientific audiences, or eager to build this skill with coaching

  • Experience giving direct, constructive feedback, such as through case reviews, shadowing, or mentoring

  • Experience turning recurring questions or feedback into clear written content, such as help articles or runbooks

  • Experience working across teams like Product, Engineering, or Professional Services to resolve issues

  • BS or M.Sc. in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Genetics, or similar life science field

Nice to have

  • Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS) practice: capturing and improving knowledge articles as part of solving issues

  • Experience working with outside partners, consultants, or implementation teams

  • A scientific background, through a life science degree or work in scientific settings

  • Experience using data to show whether training worked

Benchling welcomes everyone.

We believe diversity enriches our team so we hire people with a wide range of identities, backgrounds, and experiences.

We are an equal opportunity employer. That means we don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We also consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law, including but not limited to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.
